5.37.1.title: Back to full speed
highlights: Fixed: after a graphics hiccup the app could stay slow until it was reinstalled. It now tries the graphics card again after a day.

5.37.0.title: Easier navigating
highlights: Back now returns you to the same spot in the list, with your search, filter and scroll position kept, and there's a new Forward button (also Alt+Right).
Clicking a game's name opens its page, like the Browse button.
The window is now titled ARMGDDN Browser.

5.36.3.title: No more frozen prompts
highlights: Fixed: the app could appear frozen when a "new version" prompt popped up behind the window. Prompts now appear on top and never lock the app.

5.36.2.title: Website and app, working together
highlights: The website's Open ARMGDDN Browser button now brings the app forward.
The app lets the website know when you've switched back to the classic window, so the website only goes informational for people using the new window.

5.36.1.title: 3D covers note
highlights: 3D Printer Models now says that many models don't have a cover picture yet, and that missing covers there are expected.

5.36.0.title: Admin, tidied up
highlights: New Console tab for owners, with the website's owner commands.
Every bar chart now shows its number.
Reports show full game names, and members appear as @name or ID (click to copy).
Fixed: the PC or PCVR badge was hidden on long titles.

5.35.1.title: No more lock-ups
highlights: Fixed: the window locking up after running a long time. If it stops responding, it now recovers by itself after a few seconds, and it writes down what was going on so we can find the cause.

5.35.0.title: ARMGDDN Browser, PC or VR
highlights: Home cards, including Hidden Gems, now show a PC or PCVR badge.
When the new window is on for you, your desktop and Start Menu shortcuts are named ARMGDDN Browser.

5.34.0.title: Safer Links and Covers
highlights: A link on a website can no longer sign you in as someone else. Adding a reading order to your Komga now asks first.
Pictures from other sites are checked before they load, so a bad link cannot reach into your home network.
Admins: restarts, resets, bans and admin-list changes are confirmed in a system window.
The app turns off developer features it never uses, and your saved sign-in is readable only by your own account.

5.33.0.title: Clearer Charts
highlights: Admin charts say what each bar means, show the values and the peak, and the last row of chart cards is centered.
Desert Dusk no longer cuts off the Logout button.

5.32.0.title: Admin Polish
highlights: Admin pages show sizes as GB and TB, and dates and decades in plain form. The testing weeks now say which weeks they are.
Save any Admin page as a PDF, and a back-to-top button appears on long pages.
Missing art has Auto-fix covers and a YouTube trailer search for each game.

5.31.0.title: Live Admin Maps
highlights: The Admin Overview has the live routing map and the service map, with moving dots that follow the traffic.
The Requests tab has the request flow map, and Overview has new Usage cards (total requests, downloads, download cache) with owner Reset buttons.
The Admin tab row is visible again, and times in Admin tables show as dates.

5.30.1.title: Tidier Layout
highlights: The owner status strip no longer leaves a gap above the What's New box, no longer covers its Got it button, and no longer hides messages.
Settings, Tools and Admin now scroll inside their own box, so the status strip stays at the bottom of the window.
On Comics, the Marvel and DC collections now scroll with the list.

5.30.0.title: The Owner's Dock
highlights: Owners get a status strip along the bottom of every page: Status, Overhead, Loop, Streams, Users, Speed and Queue, with 30-minute graphs.
Click Status for the site status window. Click Streams, Users, Speed or Queue for their details. Click Loop or the System title for the analytics report.
Owner view in Settings hides the Admin tab and the dock so you can see the app as a regular member.
Admin: re-fetch all game art, with progress. It asks you to confirm first.
Admin: add or remove admins, ban a member by Telegram ID, look up a member, reload the art overrides, and set a cover or a YouTube trailer.

5.29.0.title: Admin, Built In
highlights: Owners and admins get a new Admin tab in the top bar. It never shows for anyone else.
Overview, Analytics, Music and Comics, and Reliability: the site's reports, with charts, inside the app.
System, Activity, Queue, Requests, Audit, Missing art and IP bans: the same pages as the website's panel.
Controls: reset the mirror quota and restart the server. Every action asks you to confirm first.
Requests can have their status changed from the app, and missing art can be marked "stop listing".

5.28.0.title: More From The Website, Built In
highlights: Tell me when it is added: a watchlist inside the app. You get a Telegram message when a title is added or a newer build appears.
Newest and Older tags when the same game is in two builds.
Search suggests the closest titles when you mistype, and says when a title is also in another section.
Comics show their proper title, issue number, release date and a ComicVine tag, in release order.
Publisher collections (Marvel, DC) have a Download All button at the top of Comics, under the Komga box.
Sections at quota are dimmed, and folders that point to the other server say which one to use.
The Wiki is rewritten for the app.
Help > About shows the version and can copy the details.

5.27.0.title: A Tidier Settings Page
highlights: Settings are now grouped into cards by topic: Updates, Folders, Downloads, Your games, The app and its window, Import, and Help and reports.

5.26.3.title: Easier Updating
highlights: When "Check for updates" in Settings finds a new version, the button becomes "Update to vX" and installs it.
The "Update now" bar was drawn at the very bottom of the page, out of sight. It now shows at the top, under the header.
The Settings page background is one smooth backdrop from top to bottom instead of tiled stripes.

5.26.2.title: Fixes And A Proper Menu
highlights: Fixes the Requests page, which froze the new built-in window.
A page that runs into a problem now shows a message with Try again and Back instead of freezing the app.
File > Exit now really exits.
The File menu now has Settings, Check for updates and a switch between the new and classic windows. Help has Open the log folder.
The Music and Comics "some items may be missing" notice now shows in those libraries.

5.26.1.title: Back And Forth
highlights: Every screen in the new built-in window now has a Back button, and Alt+Left or your mouse's back button works too.
In "Check my games", each game with a newer version is now a link that opens it in the library.

5.26.0.title: Easier To Get Around
highlights: The new built-in window now has a toolbar that stays the same on every page, with the page you're on highlighted.
Each page's own controls are in a second bar below it.
Every list can be shown as a grid with art, or as a plain list of titles.
The A to Z jump bar sits in the right place, and empty lists no longer show a loading spinner.

5.25.1.title: Art For 3D Models And Apps
highlights: 3D model and PC app pictures now show in the new built-in window.

5.25.0.title: Stay Up To Date
highlights: The Companion now checks for updates once an hour and tells you when one is ready, even when it's sitting in the tray.
The new built-in window has a Check for updates button in Settings.
The new built-in window now has everything the classic window had: the download schedule, game update checks, the .7z help video, What's New and clearing your history.
Members on the new window see "ARMGDDN Browser" while it updates.

5.24.2.title: Opens The Right Window
highlights: Opening the Companion again, or clicking its tray icon, now brings up the new built-in window for members who use it, instead of the old one.

5.24.1.title: Better Game Art
highlights: Game, music and comic art in the new built-in window now fits like on the website, instead of being cut off.
Internal update files are no longer listed.

5.24.0.title: Komga on the Comics Tab
highlights: The new built-in window's Comics tab now starts with a Komga section: download Komga, open the setup guide, or add a suggested reading order to your own Komga.

5.23.1.title: Small Fixes
highlights: Fixes the introduction animation in the new built-in window, which is only switched on for a few members while it is being tested. It now plays only after a first sign-in, and not for anyone who is already signed in or has seen it on the website.
The new built-in window's Settings now has Minimize to the tray and Start minimized, like the classic window.

5.23.0.title: Add to My Komga Works Again
highlights: Add to My Komga now works with current Komga versions. Komga changed how it answers when a reading order is matched against your library, which made every add report that nothing matched.

Comics are now matched to your own files exactly (the same file name and size, then the Comic Vine issue), the way the ARMGDDN reading orders are built. A reading order comes out in the right order with the right editions, even when your Komga has several series with the same name. Anything you do not have is left out and counted in the message after the add.

5.22.3.title: Smoother Long Downloads
highlights: Download links are now renewed just before they expire, so very long downloads no longer hit a burst of failed requests when a link runs out.
Retry causes in download reports are now more specific, so the reason a download slows or drops can be pinned down. No file names or paths are included.

5.22.2.title: Download Diagnostics
highlights: Download reports now include a short cause for each retry (for example a reset connection), so the reason a download slows or drops can be pinned down.

5.22.1.title: Download Diagnostics
highlights: When a download is interrupted or has to retry, the Companion now tells the site why (for example a stalled connection) so slow downloads can be found and fixed. No file names or paths are included.

5.22.0.title: Comics Keep Their Folders
highlights: Comics now download with their collection and series folders, so Komga sees each series as its own series.
Downloading several collections at once is now named "Comics" instead of after the first comic in the list.
"Only what I'm missing" puts new comics back into the right collection folder inside your comics folder.
Comics you downloaded before this update are unchanged. Delete the folder and download again to get the new layout.

5.21.3.title: Linux Fix
highlights: Fixed a crash on some Linux desktops when a download finished and a notification was shown.

5.21.2.title: Faster Recovery
highlights: Downloads now recover from a frozen connection in about 20 seconds instead of a minute. A server that is just making you wait is left alone.

5.21.1.title: Fixes
highlights: Fixed the Check for game updates button in Download History, which did nothing.
The progress bar in the Installing the update window now moves while an update installs.

5.21.0.title: Smarter Downloads
highlights: Connections per file on Auto now adjusts by itself. If your connection freezes, the next files start with fewer connections, and it goes back to normal an hour after the last freeze.
New Quiet hours in Settings: choose days and times to pause downloads or slow them to a speed you pick. Paused downloads carry on by themselves when the window ends.
New Check for game updates in Download History: lists games you've downloaded that have a newer version in the library.

5.20.0.title: Test Your Connection
highlights: A new Test my connection button in Settings checks your connection to the download server and suggests the best Connections per file setting. It takes about a minute, uses your internet briefly, and saves nothing.
Logs you send to staff now include a short summary of your download settings, so problems are quicker to diagnose.

5.19.1.title: Steadier Downloads
highlights: Downloads now recover faster when your connection stalls. If every connection to the server freezes at once, the app starts a fresh connection instead of waiting on the frozen one.
Connections that are no longer needed are now closed more reliably. This is meant to reduce a rare crash that could close the app by surprise.

5.19.0.title: Connections per File
highlights: A new setting, Connections per file, lets you choose how many connections each big file opens. If your downloads keep pausing for a moment and then carrying on, especially on Wi-Fi, try a lower number such as 4 or 2.
It's under Settings, below Max Concurrent Downloads. It's set to Auto by default, so nothing changes unless you pick a number.

5.18.1.title: Stability Update
highlights: The app's built-in engine is updated to a newer version, with the latest security fixes.
This is meant to fix a rare crash that could close the app by surprise, mostly seen on Linux.
Nothing else changes: your settings and downloads work as before.

5.18.0.title: Downloads Work Through a Proxy
highlights: Large downloads now work through an HTTP proxy. Before, big files ignored your proxy and could fail or hang on PCs that can only reach the internet through one.

To turn it on, set the HTTPS_PROXY setting on your PC, then close the Companion completely and open it again. On Windows: press Start, type "environment variables" and open "Edit environment variables for your account". Under User variables press New, type HTTPS_PROXY as the name and your proxy address as the value, for example http://127.0.0.1:8080, then press OK. (Or open Command Prompt and run: setx HTTPS_PROXY "http://127.0.0.1:8080")

If your proxy needs a login, put it in the address: http://username:password@127.0.0.1:8080. To keep certain sites off the proxy, add a NO_PROXY setting listing them, separated by commas. To turn the proxy off, delete the HTTPS_PROXY setting. Some VPN and proxy programs already set it for you. SOCKS proxies are not supported.

On Mac, open Terminal and run: HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8080 "/Applications/ARMGDDN Companion.app/Contents/MacOS/ARMGDDN Companion". On Linux, run the AppImage the same way: HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8080 ./ARMGDDN.Companion-5.18.0-x86_64.AppImage (use the file name you downloaded).

5.17.1.title: Clearer Proxy Problems
highlights: If your PC is set to use a proxy or VPN program that isn't running, downloads now say so clearly and retry without it, instead of failing.

5.17.0.title: Faster, Steadier Downloads
highlights: Downloads can now connect to a second, dedicated download address, which avoids the connection limits that were occasionally resetting downloads. If that address can't be reached, the app uses the usual one automatically. Nothing changes for you to set up.

5.16.6.title: Downloads Keep Going Through Dropouts
highlights: If your internet cuts out more than once during a download, the app now picks it back up each time, instead of giving up after the first resume. Handy on connections that drop now and then, like satellite internet.

5.16.5.title: Starts Without a Downloads Folder
highlights: The app no longer refuses to open if your Windows account has no Downloads folder. It now falls back to your Documents folder, then your home folder, to put the ARMGDDN downloads folder in.

5.16.4.title: Send Log Works Signed Out
highlights: "Send log to staff" no longer fails if your sign-in has expired, and if it can't send, it now tells you what went wrong.

5.16.3.title: Music and Comics Keep You Signed In
highlights: "Only what I'm missing" no longer asks you to start over after the app restarts or sits idle for a day or two.

5.16.2.title: Smoother Updates
highlights: Updating no longer fails or restarts on top of itself if you open the app while it installs. The download bar now fills while the update downloads. A small window now shows while the update installs, and the app reopens by itself.

5.16.0.title: Send Your Log to Staff
highlights: If staff ask for your log, open Settings, then Setup Check, and press "Send log to staff". It removes your name, file paths, emails and IP addresses, then gives you a short code to paste in the support chat. Tulip reads the log from the code.

5.15.2.title: Clearer Download Errors
highlights: When a download fails, the Companion now says what really happened. A dropped connection no longer shows as an expired link, and a crash of the download engine is called a crash.
If a VPN, proxy or security program interferes with the secure connection to the download server, the Companion now says so and what to try.
Includes the latest Electron security updates.

5.15.1.title: Steadier on Linux
highlights: If the Companion closes itself twice in a row when it starts because of a graphics driver problem, it now switches to software rendering by itself instead of crashing again.

5.15.0.title: Downloads Check Themselves
highlights: "Check files after download" is now on. Each download is compared with the original's checksums before anything is unpacked, and a damaged file is named. It reads each file once, so a big game adds a few minutes. It's switched on once for everyone; if you turn it off in Settings, it stays off.
Fixed a rare download problem. If the connection dropped while the disk was slow to save, a retry could write over part of the file. The file ended up the right size but failed to extract.
When an extracted file turns out damaged, the Companion now says which file failed its check and points you to Check files, instead of showing "wrong password".

5.14.0.title: Only What I'm Missing, Folder by Folder
highlights: Every artist, album, collection and series folder on the Music and Comics pages now has its own Only what I'm missing button. It opens the Companion and compares just that folder with yours, so you can fill in one artist or one series without scanning the whole library.
The Music panel can switch back to the whole library with one click.

5.13.0.title: Music: Only What I'm Missing
highlights: A new Music button finds the music you don't have. Pick your music folder, and the Companion compares it with the library on your PC (nothing about your folder is sent) and shows how many albums are complete, partly there, or missing.

Download what I'm missing saves just those tracks into your music folder with the library's folder layout. Nothing in that folder is unpacked, and cancelling removes only the files that download wrote.
The Music page on the site has an Only what I'm missing button that opens it.

5.12.1.title: Comics Scan Checks Sign-in
highlights: The comics scan now checks that you're signed in before it starts, and tells you what to do if you're not. Without that it would open every file, which takes hours on a cloud or network drive.
When a scan finishes it shows how many comics were matched by name and size without being opened.

5.12.0.title: Faster Comics Scan
highlights: Scanning a comics folder is much faster when it holds comics from the library, even on a cloud or network drive like R:. The Companion matches them by name and size instead of opening every file.
Files it doesn't recognise are still read, and damaged or cut-short comics are still caught.
Check my setup now tells you when your comics folder is slow to read, such as a network or cloud drive.

5.11.0.title: Comics Go Straight Into Your Folder
highlights: Download what I'm missing now saves the comics straight into the comics folder you picked, using the library's folder layout.
Your own files are never unpacked or touched. Only the new comics are added.

5.10.0.title: Only What I'm Missing
highlights: Comics: pick your comics folder and the Companion shows which comics from a reading order you don't have yet, then downloads only those.
Your folder is read on your PC and nothing about it is sent to the site.
Damaged or cut-short comic files are flagged and re-downloaded.

5.9.0.title: Progress You Can See
highlights: The progress bar now shows file checking and extracting as they happen, with a percentage, both in the Companion and in the site's downloads panel.
Checking files is measured by how much data has been read, so a big game's bar moves steadily instead of sitting on a file count.

5.8.0.title: Setup Check on Linux and Mac
highlights: Check my setup now works properly on Linux and Mac. It checks your download drive's format, warns about folders that cause trouble, and on Linux flags a setting many games need.
On a Mac it also checks that the Companion is in Applications and that Rosetta is installed.
Copy report for Tulip includes these results, so she can help Linux and Mac members without Windows advice.

5.7.0.title: Check Your Files
highlights: New Check files button on finished downloads and in History: it compares every file with the originals' checksums and tells you which one, if any, is damaged.
New setting, Check files after download: files are checked before anything is extracted, so a bad file is reported instead of being unpacked.
The Downloads panel on the site shows the result and has its own link to start a check. A check can take a few minutes on big downloads.

If Auto extract is on without Check files after download, the Check files button is hidden, because files would be unpacked before anything checked them. You'll be told once; turn the setting on to get both.

5.6.0.title: ARMGDDN Companion is Live
highlights: The Beta label is gone: ARMGDDN Companion is now the official app.

Pause and Resume now keep your progress on large files, and downloads that fail partway (expired link, dropped connection, mirror change) continue from where they stopped instead of starting the file over.
Check my setup now warns you if your download folder is the root of a drive (like D:\) and suggests a short plain folder instead.
Copy for Tulip now tells you to paste your report code in the ARMGDDN Games Welcome & Support chat.
If the download engine crashes on your PC, the Companion now says so and suggests what to try, instead of wrongly saying the link expired.
Updating the Companion now keeps your Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts.
Under-the-hood security updates.

5.5.4.title: Setup Reports Go to Beta
highlights: Copy for Tulip now directs setup reports to the ARMGDDN Beta chat, and Tulip redirects reports pasted into the main chat.

5.5.3.title: More Read Lists
highlights: Add to My Komga now works for every reading order on the Comics page, including new ones as they are added.

5.5.2.title: Fresh Read Lists
highlights: Adding a read list to Komga again now replaces the one you already have, so you can always grab a fresh copy after adding more comics.

5.5.1.title: Komga Fix
highlights: Fixed Add to My Komga showing 'Could not get the read list from ARMGDDN'.

5.5.0.title: Read Lists for Komga
highlights: On the Comics page, the new Add to My Komga buttons send a complete reading order (Marvel, DC, Batman, Daredevil, Spider-Man or Superman) straight to your own Komga server.
The first time, the app asks for your Komga address and an API key. They stay on your PC and are only used to talk to your Komga.

5.4.2.title: Smaller Fixes
highlights: On Windows, shutting down, signing out or closing the Companion while a download is running is no longer reported as a failed download.
Fixed a crash on Mac that could happen if the app was opened from the Dock while it was still starting.
Downloads of many small files, like a music album, now show an average speed instead of 'Peak: 0 bp/s' when no peak could be measured.

5.4.0.title: Landscape & TV
highlights: The Android app now works in landscape, with two columns on wide screens.
You can use it with a TV remote or game controller. The selected button lights up.
The app is now set up for Android TV and Meta Quest. Android TV is tested; Quest is not yet tested on a real headset.
The app finally has the ARMGDDN skull icon instead of the default Android robot, including the round style and the themed style on Android 13 and newer.

5.3.1.title: A Steadier Finish
highlights: Fixed a rare crash that could happen when a download finished just as the Companion window was closing.

5.3.0.title: Share My Setup
highlights: After Check my setup, a new button copies a short report you can paste in the ARMGDDN chat so Tulip can help from real facts.
The report leaves out your name, folder names and anything private. It holds the check results and recent warnings from the app's log.

5.2.0.title: Check My Setup
highlights: A new button in Settings, Check my setup, looks at the things behind most install and launch problems before you download.
It checks free space on your download drive and your Windows temp drive, your download folder's location, your antivirus, and the redistributables games need.
Each line says what is fine and what to fix. If redistributables are missing, it points you to /redists in the ARMGDDN chat.

5.1.0.title: A Clearer Low-Space Warning
highlights: If your download folder is on another drive, the low-space box now says so: your download folder is fine.
It explains that setup always unpacks its temporary files into the Windows temp folder (C: by default), wherever you save or install the game.
It links to a new Wiki guide for moving your temp folder to another drive.

5.0.26.title: Tidier Linux Installs
highlights: The Linux install command now saves the app to ~/Applications instead of your Downloads folder, and running it again updates the same file.
Website downloads now work when the app is in a folder with a space in its name. Before, the link between the website and the app silently did nothing.
The leftover .old backup after an in-app update is now cleaned up automatically.
Thanks to Dirk for the suggestion.

5.0.25.title: A Clear Message If You Left The Group
highlights: If your account is no longer in the ARMGDDN group, downloads can't start. The app now says so and tells you how to fix it, instead of showing "session expired".
To fix it: rejoin the group, complete the CAPTCHA Rose sends you within an hour, then retry the download.
The website shows the same message as soon as you click Download.

5.0.24.title: Clearer Download Errors
highlights: When a download stopped without a clear reason, the app could show a meaningless startup message as the cause. It now shows the normal "Download failed" message with an error code instead.
If you need to report a failed download, include that code and the game name so we can find the cause faster.
Messages for expired links, full disks and dropped connections are unchanged.

5.0.23.title: Auto-Extract Finds a Way
highlights: Auto-extract now works on Linux systems where the app's built-in unpacking tool refuses to start. If it can't run, the app tries a private copy of it, and then the 7-Zip already installed on your system.
If no unpacking tool can start, the app now says so plainly and tells you to install 7-Zip from your package manager, instead of "Failed to validate archive contents."
The app's log now records exactly why an extraction fails, so problems are quicker to track down.
Thanks to Dirk for the detailed testing.

5.0.22.title: Auto-Extract Works on Linux
highlights: Fixed auto-extract on some Linux and Mac installs. On 5.0.21, extraction could still fail with "Failed to validate archive contents" even though the tool was bundled, because the system wouldn't let the app run it from where it was installed. The app now falls back to running its own copy from its data folder.
Windows is unchanged. Extraction already worked there.

5.0.21.title: Auto-Extract Fixed
highlights: Fixed auto-extract. If you were on 5.0.18, 5.0.19 or 5.0.20, extracting your downloads inside the app failed with "Failed to validate archive contents before extraction." A packaging mistake on our side left out the tool the app uses to unpack archives. It's back, and this update puts it in place again.
If the unpacking tool is ever missing, the app now says so plainly and asks you to report it, instead of showing a confusing validation error.
Thanks to seb for reporting it.

5.0.20.title: Newer Engine, Clearer Drive Errors
highlights: Updated the app's built-in browser engine to its newest major version, with the latest security fixes from Chromium. Everything works the same.
Mac users: this version needs macOS 13 or newer. Macs on macOS 12 simply won't be offered the update and can keep using their current version.

If the drive you picked for downloads isn't connected (an unplugged external drive, say), the app now tells you which drive is missing and to reconnect it or choose another download folder, instead of a generic "can't create the folder" error.

5.0.19.title: Android App Update
highlights: The Android app has been rebuilt on the latest Android app framework, with security updates throughout. Login, layout and downloads were tested on a real phone.
Nothing changes in the desktop app. This update is for Android users.

5.0.18.title: Safer and Clearer
highlights: Updated the app's built-in browser engine to its latest security release, picking up 11 rounds of Chromium security fixes.
If your antivirus quarantines the download engine, the app now tells you how to restore it and exclude the app's folder, instead of just saying it failed to start.
Checking for updates no longer shows a confusing error when GitHub is busy. The app just asks you to try again in a little while.

5.0.17.title: Quieter Behind the Scenes
highlights: Cleaned up how the app reports problems back to us. Everyday hiccups, like an expired download link, a rate limit, or your connection dropping, no longer count as bugs, so the real ones stand out and get fixed faster.
Nothing changes in how downloads work. This update is just housekeeping.

5.0.16.title: Fewer Failed Downloads
highlights: If a download fails because your internet dropped, the app now waits for your connection to come back and resumes it automatically. No more coming back to a failed download that just needed a Retry.

Before a download starts, the app now checks the drive your Windows temp folder is on (usually C:). The game's setup unpacks its temp files there even when you install elsewhere. If there isn't enough room, it warns you up front instead of after the download finishes.

If your PC's date/time is wrong, or your antivirus is scanning secure connections, downloads can't connect. The app now tells you exactly that and how to fix it, instead of failing with a vague error.
Cancelling or pausing a download no longer shows a "Download failed" message.
Fixed a crash when opening the app while it was closing.

5.0.15.title: Smoother Installs
highlights: Auto-extract now unpacks games straight into the download folder, like 7-Zip's "Extract here", instead of into an extra subfolder. That extra folder could make file paths too long for Windows, and setup would then "finish" instantly with nothing installed.
If your C: drive doesn't have enough free space for a game's installer, the app now tells you when the download finishes. Setup unpacks to C: first even when you install the game somewhere else.

5.0.14.title: Riding Out Connection Drops
highlights: If your internet drops for a moment during a download, the app now waits for it to come back (up to 5 minutes) and carries on, instead of failing right away.
Fixed large multi-part games failing on their later parts with "Download link expired". Each part now gets its own fresh links when it needs them.

5.0.13.title: Recovering From Dropped Connections
highlights: If your connection to a mirror drops partway through a file, the app now switches to another mirror and carries on, instead of failing the download.
Error reports now include the recovery steps the app tried, so we can fix stuck downloads faster.

5.0.12.title: Honest Speed Limits
highlights: Max Concurrent Downloads now goes up to 6, the most the server allows per user. If you had it set higher, it's been set to 6 for you. You won't lose any speed, because the extra slots were never being used.
Fixed a misleading "Server load is high" warning that showed up even when the server wasn't busy, for anyone with the setting above 6.

5.0.11.title: Smarter Mirror Switching
highlights: If a mirror is rate-limiting a file or has hit its download limit, the app now switches to another mirror automatically instead of failing.
Fixed downloads that could fail with "Download link expired" when the real problem was one busy mirror. The app now tries a different mirror before giving up.

5.0.10.title: Fits Every Screen
highlights: Fixed Settings being cut off at the top and bottom on ultra-wide and short screens. It now scrolls, so every option is reachable.
Behind the scenes: crash reports now include a little more detail about graphics issues, so they're easier to fix.

5.0.9.title: Clean Exits
highlights: Fixed a crash that could happen when closing the app while a download was still running.

5.0.8.title: No More Graphics Crashes
highlights: Fixed the app closing itself on some PCs because of a graphics driver problem. If your graphics card can't keep up, the app now switches to a safe drawing mode and keeps running.
You won't notice any difference in how the app looks or works in the safe mode.

5.0.7.title: Better Bug Hunting
highlights: The app now sends an automatic error report when something goes wrong, like a crash or a download that fails, so problems get spotted and fixed without you having to report them.
Reports are stripped of personal info before they're sent: no download links or tokens, no IP address, and your user folder name is hidden.
Prefer not to send them? Turn off "Send error reports" in Settings.

5.0.6.title: Back on Its Feet
highlights: Fixed downloads that could freeze partway through a file and sit there forever. If a connection dies mid-download, the app now notices within about a minute instead of never.
Stalled files now retry automatically with a fresh link, up to 3 times, before giving up. No more restarting a download by hand just because your connection hiccuped.
If a file still can't be resumed after those retries, the error now says so clearly instead of the misleading "stalled at 0 B/s".

5.0.5.title: Unstuck
highlights: Found and fixed a real bug where downloads could quietly stop making progress partway through, especially after a retry or a pause — the app would still say it was downloading, but nothing was actually happening.
Added better internal diagnostics so if a download ever does stall again, we'll be able to see exactly why instead of guessing.

5.0.4.title: Fixed a Download That Wouldn't Stay Finished
highlights: Fixed a bug where a download recovering from an expired link could get wrongly marked as failed while it was actually still finishing — the app would then look like it "restarted" a completed download. Thanks to Kaizo for reporting this one with logs, which made it possible to track down.
Downloads should now recover cleanly from expired links and mirror switches without any UI weirdness.

5.0.2.title: Space, Mirrors, Priority
highlights: Free space is now shown in Settings and while downloads are running — you'll get a warning if space gets tight mid-download instead of finding out the hard way.
Mirror auto-switching now catches a few more failure types, and you'll actually see it happen ("Switched mirrors ×2") instead of it being invisible.
Drag a queued download to the top of the list to have it start first.
This popup! You'll see what changed right after every update from now on.

5.0.0.title: A Fresh Coat of Neon
highlights: The whole app got a visual revamp — same neon look, cleaner everywhere.
Status badges are now color-coded so you can tell downloading/completed/failed/paused apart at a glance.
Settings panel got restyled toggle switches and a proper dropdown.
Toast notifications for things like "Settings saved" and "History cleared".
